## How I verified completeness

- `@app.route(` count: 9; `@ollama_app.route(` count: 12; total 21 — matches the line-by-line grep.
- Grep for `@app.get/post/put/delete/patch`, `add_url_rule`, `Blueprint`, `register_blueprint`, `errorhandler`, `@after_request` (as a route) in `nollama.py`: **zero hits**. The only other `@app.`/`@ollama_app.` members are two `@before_request` hooks (lines 5202, 5727), which are not routes.
- Only two `Flask(...)` instances in the file (lines 4688, 5723); no sub-apps, no blueprints, no dynamic registration.
- No path parameters (`<id>` etc.) anywhere; all paths are literal.
- Note: the grep for `@app.route` also hits in `docs/archive/WEB-UI-PLAN.md` and `docs/archive/OLLAMA-API-PLAN.md` — those are documentation/plan snippets, not live code.

## Conditional registration — and an important nuance

**All 21 routes are registered unconditionally at import time.** None are registered inside an `if`, and no route exists conditionally on flags or devices. What *is* conditional is **serving**:

- `app` (the 9 OpenAI-port routes) is always served on `args.port` (line 7195, main thread).
- `ollama_app` (the 12 Ollama-port routes) is only put on the wire **if `args.ollama_port` is truthy** (lines 7179–7191, background daemon thread). If `--ollama-port` is `0`/omitted the app is never started. Additionally, if that port is already in use the flag is forced to `0` (lines 6933–6939) and the Ollama app is silently not served — so the 12 Ollama routes can be unreachable even though they're registered.
- Related: this is why the OpenAI-port app deliberately *also* serves the Ollama-shaped embedding routes (`/api/embed`, `/api/embeddings`) and why the Ollama-port app also serves `/v1/chat/completions` — the comment block at lines 5405–5409 and the docstring at 6230 explain this cross-port duplication (a client configured with one base URL must get embeddings/chat even if only one port exists).

A few more observations worth noting:

- The two routes with no explicit `methods=` (`/` on both apps, lines 5212 and 5733) default to **GET only** (HEAD/OPTIONS remain implicit per Flask).
- Runtime (not registration) conditions inside handlers: `/v1/audio/transcriptions` returns 503 if no whisper slot is configured; the three embedding routes return 503 if no embed slot is ready; `/api/pull`, `/api/delete`, `/api/copy` are intentional stubs (lines 6208–6225) that exist only because clients probe for them.
- `/v1/chat/completions` on the Ollama app (6229) is a thin delegate that calls the same `chat_completions()` handler as the OpenAI app (6232 → 5475).
